key_insight: Noise-biased qudits can dramatically reduce the overhead of dynamical decoupling, extending the coherence of highly nonclassical states in a spin-8 system.
engineering_relevance: This points to a practical route for longer-lived logical qubits in qudit-based quantum hardware by tailoring control sequences to the system’s noise structure.
method: Implemented dynamical decoupling on a model d=8 qudit: the nuclear spin of an antimony donor in silicon.
Benchmarked sequences on uniform superpositions, cat states, and Haar-random states.
Used continuous DD for a spin-cat error-correction code to protect a logical superposition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coherence improvements of roughly 5x–10x, with logical |+>_L coherence extended to 225 ms versus 19 ms under free evolution and 85 ms with a Hahn echo.
watch_item: The demonstrated overhead reduction depends on favorable noise bias, so performance may not generalize to less biased or more complex qudit platforms.
paper_title: Dynamical Decoupling of Nonclassical States in a Biased-Noise Spin Qudit
